name: Polar
summary: A payments platform for developers that acts as the merchant of record.

free_plan_covers.note: No monthly fee or size limit on the free Starter plan; you pay 5% plus 50 cents per transaction instead.

first_paid_usd_month.note: There is no required monthly plan; the free Starter plan has no cap, though optional paid plans (Pro at $20/month, Growth at $100/month, Scale at $400/month) lower the per-transaction fee at higher sales volume.

portability.note: Polar is a proprietary merchant-of-record checkout like Lemon Squeezy, so switching away later means rebuilding checkout, subscriptions and tax setup somewhere else.

merchant_of_record.note: Polar is the merchant of record on every sale, handling sales tax and VAT for you.

subscriptions.note: Recurring subscription billing is a core Polar feature, with no separate subscription fee on the current Starter, Pro, Growth or Scale plans.

fee_summary.value: 5% + 50 cents per transaction on the free Starter plan
fee_summary.note: Paid monthly plans lower this rate, down to 3.4% plus 30 cents per transaction on the $400/month Scale plan, and international cards add 1.5%.

card_fee_percent.note: Polar keeps 5% of each US card payment, as listed on its pricing page.

card_fee_fixed_usd.note: On top of the percent, Polar keeps $0.50 from each US card payment.

setup.step: Create a Polar account and a test organization in the sandbox at sandbox.polar.sh, which is fully separate from production data, and add a product to sell.
Generate an Organization Access Token from Settings > Developers and set it as an environment variable.
Install the SDK with npm install zod @polar-sh/nextjs.
Create a checkout route handler using Checkout from @polar-sh/nextjs with server set to sandbox, and a webhook route handler using Webhooks verified against a signing secret.
Visit your checkout route and complete a test payment with a Stripe test card number inside the sandbox.

builder_notes: Keep POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN and POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET server-only and never prefix them with NEXT_PUBLIC_.
Build and test against server: "sandbox" and the sandbox.polar.sh dashboard, and only point at production once you are ready to take real payments.
Verify the POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET signature inside the webhook handler before granting access, instead of trusting the client-side checkout redirect alone.
